title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Select batch-invariant matmul configs from runtime M

# [Bugfix] Select batch-invariant matmul configs from runtime M under `torch.compile`

Fixes #54243.

## Problem

The tuned batch-invariant matmul table is keyed by `(architecture, N, K, M bucket)`,
but Dynamo evaluates the Python lookup while tracing. The resulting Triton tile is
therefore fixed in a dynamic graph even though `M` remains a runtime value.

## What this changes

- Route only compiled BF16 shapes that have tuned table entries through a vLLM
  custom op. Its implementation runs after tracing and selects the tile from the
  actual runtime `M`.
- Keep eager execution, FP16/FP32, architectures without a table, and untuned
  `(N, K)` shapes on the existing path.
- Prewarm the reach

At `page_size=1` this is a per-token envelope. Co-locating a page's whole depth is a building block for page-granular K

title: [Deterministic] Support TP-Invariant Inference
body_opening:
## Motivation

In RL training, the rollout engine and the training engine often use different tensor parallel sizes. Rollout engines (e.g. SGLang) typically use larger TP (e.g. TP=8) to maximize throughput, while training engines such as FSDP use TP=1 for better memory efficiency. This TP size mismatch leads to noticeable numerical gaps in predicted probabilities between rollout and training, introducing a training–inference mismatch that can undermine on-policy RL and harm stability.

This PR integrates [Tree Based Invariant Kernels (TBIK)](https://tbik.super.site/) to ensure bit-wise deterministic results across different TP sizes, eliminating TP induced numerical discrepancies.

title: [Feature] Add rolling-hash repetition detection algorithm
body_opening:
Adds an opt-in `algorithm="rolling_hash"` option to `RepetitionDetectionParams` (added in #35451). The default stays `"naive"` so nothing changes for existing users.

The naive scan has two practical issues:

1. Patterns longer than `max_pattern_size` go undetected, so the paragraph- or JSON-block-sized loops that motivate this feature in the first place often slip through unless the cap is cranked up.
2. Cranking the cap up costs O(L²·K) per step.

The rolling-hash detector uses a double polynomial hash (Mersenne 2^61-1 + 2^31-1, collision probability < 2^-90) with a two-stage filter — a single-token prune on the candidate period L (Stage 1) followed by O(K) range-hash equality on the few s

title: [Disagg] Layer-pipelined KV transfer: overlap RDMA with GPU compute
body_opening:
## Motivation

In PD disaggregation mode, KV cache transfer happens **after** full prefill computation completes. For long prompts (≥1K tokens), this creates a significant TTFT bottleneck — the decode side must wait for all layers to be computed and then transferred sequentially.

This PR implements **layer-pipelined KV transfer**: instead of computing all layers then transferring all KV at once, we split layers into groups and transfer each group incrementally. Transfer of group N overlaps with GPU compute of group N+1, significantly reducing TTFT.

Related: #19931 (same direction, different approach)
